clue.text: Do the same as prisoner with criminal record

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
in British slang a person with form has a criminal record

explanation.surface: A prisoner who has a criminal record behaves just like the other inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' is British slang for a police record, as in 'he has form'.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with a pattern, acting as others act.

clue.text: Last of air removed from high cloud and carbon injected as entertainment

indicators.note: injected means the symbol is put inside what remains
removed from means that letter comes out of the cloud's name

parts.note: cirrus is a wispy cloud found at high altitude

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of air is used

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A science experiment: air is let out of a cloud and carbon is pumped in, as a spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus is a travelling show of acrobats, clowns and animals, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Unimportant person describing a weak wine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person of no importance
second meaning, read as ...: a thin wine is said to have ...

explanation.walkthrough: Wine tasters speak of a wine's body, its fullness; a thin one has none.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no significance, a nonentity.

clue.text: Award Savage a very low mark for wit

parts.note: an Oscar is the Academy Award for films
wild means savage, untamed
E is a very low grade in an exam

explanation.surface: A reviewer gives an award but savages a performance with a dismal mark for its humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The wit is the Irish playwright famed for his epigrams.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright was renowned as one of the great conversationalists and epigram-makers, a celebrated wit.

clue.text: Old military leader is well (sadly not internally)

indicators.note: internally means the mixed letters go inside the exclamation

parts.note: well! and my! are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: sadly as in badly, unhappily arranged, so the letters of not are mixed up

explanation.surface: An old general is in good health, though not, sadly, inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is an exclamation here, MY, not 'healthy'. Monty was the nickname of Field Marshal Montgomery.
explanation.definitionFit: Monty was the nickname of Field Marshal Montgomery, the British Second World War commander.

clue.text: They put the squeeze on Hypnos, cast outside Troy

indicators.note: outside says the reworked letters of Hypnos go around the letter for Troy
cast in the sense of thrown about, so the letters of Hypnos are reshaped

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for troy, the system of weights

explanation.surface: A mythic tale: the god of sleep, Hypnos, is besieged by constrictors around the walls of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy is not the city but troy weight, abbreviated t.
explanation.definitionFit: These large snakes kill prey by constriction, coiling round and squeezing it.

clue.text: Note name assumed by wild alpine plant

indicators.note: assumed by in the sense of taken on, taken in, by the rearranged letters
wild means the letters of alpine run free in a new order

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A botanist notes the name taken by a wild mountain flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A perennial is a plant that lives for more than two years, flowering year after year.

clue.text: Shaker town holding back migration

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in the opposite direction
holding says the letters are held within the words Shaker town

explanation.surface: A town of the Shaker religious sect holds up a mass movement of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across shaKER Town and are read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long arduous journey, especially the historic migration of the Boers.

clue.text: Sailor's girlfriend with yen to yield to independence — the virgin kind?

indicators.note: to yield to means one letter gives way and another takes its place

parts.note: Olive Oyl is the girlfriend of Popeye the Sailor Man in the cartoon
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, the yen

explanation.surface: A sailor's girlfriend, with a yearning to give way to independence, is perhaps a virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: Yen looks like a longing but is the currency letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra virgin and virgin are grades of the product pressed from olives, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Seaside feature: sex initiation plus nude swimming

indicators.note: initiation means the beginning, the first letter of sex

parts.note: and means plus

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of nude move about

explanation.surface: A beach scene: a first sexual encounter and a spot of naked bathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand dune is a ridge of wind-blown sand typical of coastlines.

clue.text: In miniature, because an instrument

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a tiny object is so because it is a musical instrument in miniature.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across miniatuRE BECause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument, an ancestor of the fiddle.

clue.text: Sporting grannie almost won National

indicators.note: sporting in the sense of frolicking or playing about, so the letters are jumbled
almost means the word won loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A sporty grandmother nearly wins the Grand National horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: Take WO (almost 'won') with GRANNIE and rearrange. 'National' looks like the British horse race but is a noun meaning a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, so a Norwegian is a citizen of Norway.

clue.text: Basic failure to meet storytelling quota?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fundamental, lying beneath everything else
second meaning: telling fewer lies than required

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as under-lying: lying (telling stories, fibbing) below the target amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlying means fundamental or basic, the cause that sits beneath what is seen.

clue.text: Very numb

explanation.walkthrough: Two words read as one phrase, but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an intensifying adverb (dead right) and as an adjective for a limb lacking sensation.

clue.text: Fail to qualify? Don't go falling into the canal!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in golf, to score too poorly to play the final rounds

definitions.text: Don't go falling into the canal!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a warning to avoid falling into a cut, an old word for a canal

explanation.walkthrough: A cut is a canal in British usage; the phrase is a warning on the towpath.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the cut eliminates players after the early rounds, and those below it fail to qualify.

clue.text: Getting people to talk in a form of Inuit is nothing, without question

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters surround the letter for question
a form of says the letters are given another shape

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An interrogation conducted in a dialect of Inuit, carried out without asking any questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': IN followed by the rearranged INUIT IS O goes around Q.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquisition is a harsh interrogation, forcing prisoners to talk.

clue.text: Tending to shake, a bit like a flight case?

definitions.text: a bit like a flight case?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: somewhat like a quiver, the case holding arrows, or flights

explanation.walkthrough: A flight case sounds like luggage, but flights are arrows and their case is a quiver.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver is to tremble, and the suffix -ish gives an adjective for something inclined to tremble.

clue.text: Removes barriers as protection from the enemy

definitions.meaning: second meaning: fortifications or forces that guard against attack

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into DE and FENCES, as if a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Defences are fortifications and other means of resisting military attack.

clue.text: Set your sights on a state-backed scholarly environment

indicators.note: backed means the letters run backwards

parts.note: aimed, as in set your sights on a target
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Aim for a university funded by the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is past tense here, giving AIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Class relied on reform to get aircraft squadrons in France

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of class and relied are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A school class depended on reforms to secure military aircraft for France.
explanation.definitionFit: Escadrille is the French word for a small air-force squadron, adopted in English for French and First World War units.

clue.text: Brief from foreign leader spreading fake news

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of foreign

parts.note: lying is telling untruths, spreading fake news

explanation.surface: A short statement from a foreign head of state is full of disinformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying as in a flying visit means hasty and short-lived.

clue.text: Leave wrapping right round bird

indicators.note: wrapping means the word for leave goes around the other letters

parts.note: to part is to leave, depart
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Instructions for wrapping a present around a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The parrot is a brightly coloured tropical bird known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Current undergarment for a woman lacks opening

indicators.note: lacks opening means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a teddy is a woman's one-piece undergarment

explanation.surface: The latest women's lingerie is missing its front opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning up to date, but it is a noun: a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of water or air.

clue.text: German region we backed way before failure, some might say

indicators.note: some might say signals that the answer is how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: WE followed (backed) by ST, way as in street, and then FAILURE, said together

explanation.surface: A tale of German history: we supported a route that later collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: WE with ST behind it gives WEST; said with FAILURE it sounds like the region's name. ST is the abbreviation for street, a way.
explanation.definitionFit: Westphalia is a historic region of north-west Germany, now part of North Rhine-Westphalia.

clue.text: Armadillo's articulated body marking

indicators.note: articulated in the sense of spoken aloud, pronounced

parts.note: a tattoo is an inked marking on the skin

explanation.surface: An armadillo's jointed body has patterned markings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' looks like jointed, which suits an armadillo's armour, but means spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatou is an old name for the armadillo, especially the giant species, from a South American language.

clue.text: Southern French town's excuse, when independence lost

indicators.note: lost says the letter standing for independence goes missing from the excuse

parts.note: an alibi is an excuse

explanation.surface: A town in southern France offers an excuse for losing its independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Albi is a cathedral town in the Tarn department of south-west France.

clue.text: Disease has politician stretched out flat in bed

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MP is Member of Parliament
lain is the past participle of lie, to stretch out flat

explanation.surface: An ill politician has been lying flat in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or ailment, as in a chest complaint.

clue.text: Street seller's recipe involved with rice?

indicators.note: involved in the sense of entangled, so the letters of rice are mixed together

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A hawker shouts out his recipe for a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the prescription sign, from Latin 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crier calls out loudly in public; street criers hawked their wares by shouting.

clue.text: European bridge: one should start leading hearts

indicators.note: leading means the letter just made goes in front of the one for hearts

parts.note: a span is a bridge, or the arch of one
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: start means only the first letter of should is used

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Advice on the card game bridge: someone should open by leading a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge of the surface is the card game; here it is a span.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a European, and the adjective Spanish describes someone from Spain.

clue.text: In revolt, mean and tense

parts.note: the people are up in arms, in revolt
tight means mean, stingy with money

explanation.surface: Rebellious, stingy and stressed: a portrait of a disgruntled person.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means anxious and nervous, unable to relax.
